name: Medial approach to the distal femur (periprosthetic knee)
corridor: Straight incision along the adductor-magnus tendon, elevating vastus medialis anteriorly off sartorius, with Hunter-canal vessels protected if the cut is carried proximally

positioning.text: Position so the adductor tubercle and adductor-magnus tendon can be marked; the corridor is safe beside a healed midline TKA scar.

surface_landmarks.text: Identify the adductor tubercle and mark the adductor-magnus tendon proximally.

incision.text: Make a straight cut along the posterior border of the adductor-magnus tendon and extend it proximally as needed.

superficial_interval.text: Find the posterior border of vastus medialis distally and elevate it anteriorly, developing the plane between vastus medialis and sartorius.

deep_interval.text: Flex the knee so sartorius can be retracted posteriorly, exposing the adductor-magnus tendon to the adductor tubercle. Retract adductor magnus posteriorly and vastus medialis anteriorly onto the femur. Proximally this plane borders Hunter's canal.

layers.text: Skin, vastus medialis–sartorius interval, adductor-magnus tendon, then the medial distal femur.

structures_at_risk.text: The femoral vessels in Hunter's canal are at risk if proximal dissection is careless.

danger_zones.text: Hunter's canal, formed by sartorius as the cut is carried proximally, is the danger zone for the femoral vessels.

retraction_hazards.text: Do not injure the femoral vessels while retracting sartorius or working beside Hunter's canal.

exposure.text: Shows the medial distal femur for a medial plate or a second plate in a dual-plate construct.

limitations.text: The window is medial only. Proximal length is limited by Hunter's canal.

indications.text: Used for a medial distal-femoral periprosthetic fracture and when simultaneous medial and lateral plates are planned.

closure.text: After hemostasis, close in layers with absorbable suture and the chosen skin closure.

complications.text: The principal complication is femoral-vessel injury in Hunter's canal during proximal extension.

procedure_applications.condition: A medial distal-femoral periprosthetic fracture, or a dual-plate construct, is exposed medially beside a healed TKA scar

questions.question: Along which tendon is the incision placed?
questions.answer: The adductor-magnus tendon, after marking the adductor tubercle.

questions.question: What structure forms the border of Hunter's canal in this approach?
Is the approach safe next to a healed midline TKA scar?
